Markdown export structure: For Notion Markdown export evaluators, verify heading levels and section contents with exact line/section parsing rather than broad substring matches, and require checkbox state using case-normalized comparisons on both the pattern and line.

For Notion Markdown exports, verify task-list blocks with exact Markdown checkbox syntax and explicitly enforce bottom placement by requiring the unchecked to-do line to be the final non-empty content line, not merely after a section heading.

For Notion Markdown exports, evaluators should parse the exported .md file as a local cached vm_file path and should explicitly count expected heading levels, list blocks, and checkbox syntax to prevent extra stale or unrelated content from passing.
Markdown export page title verification: For Notion Markdown export tasks, verify the page title separately from Heading 1 blocks; Notion exports may represent both the page title and H1 blocks with Markdown '#', so evaluators should explicitly check the required page title and the required content block sequence.
Markdown export callout verification: For Notion Markdown exports, verifying callout text alone is weak; the evaluator should also check the exported callout/blockquote formatting, typically a line beginning with '>' that contains the callout text.

For Notion Markdown exports, do not give high credit for plain text when the instruction requires a callout; require the exported callout/blockquote structure or another concrete callout marker so ordinary paragraphs cannot pass.

For Notion Markdown exports, callout blocks are commonly represented as blockquote lines, often with an emoji before the text; evaluators should check for blockquote structure while allowing harmless emoji/prefix text.
Markdown export page title: For Notion Markdown export tasks, evaluators should explicitly verify the page title as well as content blocks; checking only body headings can miss a required page-title subgoal.
Markdown export verification: For Notion Markdown exports, verify the exported page title as well as block content, and enforce exact section ordering and exact list counts; otherwise a hand-written or partially correct Markdown file can receive high reward.

For Notion Markdown exports, line-based Markdown checks are appropriate, but exact-count list requirements should fail or heavily penalize extra list items in the relevant section rather than awarding high partial credit.
dependency source files in evaluators: Do not include a scoring rule that checks immutable input/source files from the task setup; it can produce positive initial reward. Use source files only to derive expected values, while scoring should depend on the user-created output artifact.
Markdown export heading verification: When a Notion task requires a Heading 1 block, the exported Markdown should be checked for an exact '# Heading Text' line; accepting '##' through '######' misses the required block level.
